name: MI-05
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+13 partisan lean favors Republican incumbent Tim Walberg
Overwhelming fundraising gap: $1.7M raised and $994K on hand for Walberg versus $56K for Democrat Christian Vukasovich
No public polls or expert ratings; prediction markets price the Republican around 94%
National environment tilts toward Democrats, providing the only offsetting factor
model.rationale: Walberg combines a comfortable R+13 district with incumbency and a roughly thirty-to-one fundraising advantage, and prediction markets price his renomination-to-reelection path near certain. With no polls available, the fundamentals point to a decisive but not untouchable Republican margin, kept below Safe R status by a national environment favoring Democrats.
model.watch: A significantly stronger Democratic national tide in the fall could compress the margin, though flipping a district this red would require a historically large shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican Tim Walberg seeks another term in Michigan's 5th District, a seat with a Republican lean of about thirteen points. He enters the general election with a decisive financial advantage, having raised roughly $1.7 million and holding nearly $1 million on hand, while Democratic nominee Christian Vukasovich has raised about $56,000. No public polls of the race are available, and no major expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Walberg roughly a ninety-four percent chance of winning, reflecting both the district's partisan makeup and his incumbency. A Green Party, Libertarian, and independent candidate are also on the ballot, though none has shown meaningful financial support. The national environment may be more favorable to Democrats than in recent cycles, which could narrow the margin somewhat, but the underlying fundamentals point firmly toward the incumbent. The race is best characterized as likely Republican.
